probes.query: Two clients concurrently change the same single-valued field of the same node. Where is the key that makes these two writes clash produced, and which component finally decides that one of them must be aborted?
expectedFacts: The clash key is built from a farm fingerprint of the data key; for a non-list predicate it is XORed with uid 0, so two different values written to the same node+predicate collide.
For list predicates the value fingerprint is XORed in, so different values do not conflict; predicates with a no-conflict schema directive produce no key.
The keys travel to the cluster coordinator (Zero) in the transaction context as base-36 strings.
Zero's Oracle aborts the commit if any key was committed at a timestamp later than the transaction's start timestamp (or the start ts is older than the leader's startTxnTs).

probes.query: Before evaluating an equality filter on a small candidate set, the engine weighs reading index entries against reading stored values directly. Where does its estimate of how many nodes match a value come from, and how is that estimate built up?
expectedFacts: The estimate comes from a per-predicate count-min sketch held by posting.StatsHolder (epsilon 0.001, delta 0.99).

The sketch is fed lazily: each time handleUidPostings reads an index posting list for a comparison function it records the list's approximate length under that token; nothing is precomputed at index time.

planForEqFilter uses the sketch: with no estimate it reads the index tokens; if the candidate list is smaller than the estimated count divided by the type-filter uid limit it fetches values directly. Lists below the limit (default 10) skip the estimate.

probes.query: How does the system decide whether a new backup is a full copy or only the changes since the previous one, and how does a restore then choose which earlier backups to replay?
expectedFacts: ProcessBackupRequest reads the latest manifest at the destination and uses its read timestamp as SinceTs; forceFull sets SinceTs to 0. Type is 'full' when SinceTs is 0, otherwise 'incremental' with BackupNum incremented under the same BackupId.
An incremental backup is refused if the new read ts does not advance past the last manifest, or if encryption is on for one side and off for the other (forceFull is the suggested escape).

getManifestsToRestore keeps only manifests whose backup files all exist, walks from the newest back to the latest full backup (optionally filtered by BackupId), and verifyManifests checks the BackupNum chain is consecutive starting at 1.

probes.query: What rule makes the cluster automatically move a field's data from one group of servers to another, and what limits stop it from thrashing?
expectedFacts: A ticker (default every 8 minutes) asks chooseTablet for a move; only the Zero leader acts and only when there is more than one group.

It moves from the largest group toward the smallest only if the size difference is at least 10% of the smallest group, choosing the largest tablet whose size is at most half the difference; reserved predicates are never chosen.
A failed move that ran at least a minute puts the tablet into a cooldown that starts at 1 hour, doubles per consecutive failure, and is capped at 24 hours; manual moves are not held back.

probes.query: Where do change-data events for external consumers come from, and why was that source chosen over subscribing to the key-value store directly?

Mutation events are held per start timestamp and sent only when the commit delta arrives, carrying the commit ts; the only sinks are Kafka and a file.

Each attempt takes weight 1<<retry from a shared limiter capped by the pending-proposals setting (default 256); commit/abort deltas skip the limiter.

probes.query: When a read needs data held by another group of servers and the first replica answers slowly, what does the calling server do?
expectedFacts: If the local node serves the group no network call is made; otherwise up to two members of the group are chosen.
The request goes to the first; if no reply arrives within one second (backupRequestGracePeriod) the same request is also sent to the second, and the first successful reply wins.
If the first fails before the grace period, the second is tried immediately.

probes.query: How does result sorting choose between walking a sorted index and fetching the values directly?
expectedFacts: processSort does not choose up front: it runs both strategies concurrently and takes the first to finish without error.
The value-fetching strategy is started only after a 3 ms delay, so a quick index sort usually wins; the loser is cancelled through the shared context.
If the first to return has an error the other result is used; sorting on list-typed predicates and negative counts are rejected beforehand.

probes.query: Why can't the write-ahead log simply be truncated up to the most recent committed entry, and what decides the safe cut point?
expectedFacts: Pre-writes of uncommitted transactions are not persisted in the main store, so their Raft entries must be kept until the transaction commits or aborts.

calculateSnapshot scans entries and sets the snapshot index just before the first mutation whose start ts is at or above the minimum pending start ts; the minimum is the smaller of the Oracle's MinPendingStartTs and the CDC tracker's oldest unsent ts.
The snapshot's ReadTs is the maximum commit timestamp seen; no snapshot is made if nothing can be discarded.
